equity_bridge.note: FY26 AR balance sheet, line 5663; charged once here, flows consolidated

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: long-run nominal growth for a luxury-led wine portfolio in a structurally declining volume category (Penfolds/Asia growth offset by US and commercial declines); the historical CAGRs are impairment- and cycle-distorted and none is a usable forward anchor
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3y CAGR (-4.8%) diverges from revenue (+1.8%) because FY26 impairments wrote A$1.45bn off book equity; owner-FCF CAGRs are meaningless (FY23 base of A$9.2m, FY26 trough of A$67.5m after a A$326m working-capital build). None of these series is used as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue FY21 2,683.9 -> FY26 2,626.0; FY23 2,488.3 -> FY26. EPS: FY21 statutory 34.6c and FY23 35.1c against FY26 UNDERLYING EPS 34.1c (statutory FY26 is -133.4c and is not comparable). Equity FY21 3,591.2 / FY23 3,878.9 -> FY26 3,348.3. Owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC, interest income not stripped): FY21 345.5, FY22 439.4, FY23 9.2, FY24 229.9, FY25 369.8, FY26 67.5. SBC is 0.4-0.7% of revenue throughout, so owner and reported FCF CAGRs are essentially identical; SBC is not consuming the growth.

scenario_narratives.base: Guidance-anchored FY27 (EBITS flat, revenue -3%, capex A$75m), then a mid-cycle margin recovery to 28% EBITDAS by FY30 as Ascent cost-out lands and Penfolds mix rises, and 2.5-3% long-run growth. Deleveraging to <2.0x by FY28 is consistent with these flows. Terminal value capped at 15x owner FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: Ascent delivers in full and Treasury Americas recovers: 31% EBITDAS margin (management's 25%+ EBITS aspiration) by FY31, mid-single-digit growth FY28-31 on Penfolds Asia and a stabilised US, working-capital release from portfolio simplification, 3% terminal growth.
scenario_narratives.bear: US keeps deteriorating and Penfolds/China disappoints or faces renewed trade barriers; revenue down ~13% cumulative by FY29, margins stuck at 24-25% EBITDAS, leverage above target beyond FY28, dividend stays suspended. Risk carried in the flows at the same 9% WACC.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the earnings power, not the FY26 statutory loss: TWE's A$1.7bn of US write-downs are sunk, and the business is a luxury-wine franchise (Penfolds) wrapped in a shrinking US and commercial portfolio. The flows are component-built from trough EBITDAS with a mid-cycle recovery, leases charged as operating cost, SBC expensed with a flat share count, cash tax at statutory, working capital consuming cash on growth, and a 15x terminal cap because wine is a structurally slow, inventory-heavy category. Risk is priced once, in the scenario paths and a 30% bear weight, at a single 9% AUD WACC. The price (near the top of its 52-week range) already discounts a good part of the Ascent recovery; the 15% hurdle entry price is where the recovery is bought with a margin of safety.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin recovery path: each 1pp of terminal EBITDAS margin is worth roughly A$0.35/share; the base assumes 28%, management targets ~31%, FY26 printed 25%
Penfolds/China concentration: ~72% of divisional EBITS from one brand; renewed Australia-China trade barriers would push the outcome toward the bear path
Treasury Americas: further distributor disruption or impairments; the FY26 write-downs removed book value but not the operating drag
Leverage: 2.8x EBITDAS with the dividend suspended; a weak FY27 cash year would delay the <2.0x target beyond FY28 and could force asset sales at poor prices
Working-capital intensity: luxury wine inventory means any re-acceleration of growth consumes cash before it shows in FCF (wc_capture -35%)
Lease treatment: valuation is on an ex-lease net debt of A$1,309m with lease cash charged in the flows; readers comparing to the company's A$1,782m headline net debt must not deduct leases again

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 3.34-6.45
data_sources.financials: TWE.AX_Metrics.csv / metrics_normalized (FY2015-FY2026 annuals and halves, AUD millions); FY2026 Annual Report (TWE.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt): KPI reconciliation lines 2200-2275 (EBITS 492.3, EBITDAS 657.5, D&A 165.2, net finance costs 107.4), cash flow statement lines 5760-5810, OCF reconciliation lines 6645-6670 (SBC 9.6, working capital), note 11 leases lines 7033-7100 (ROU depreciation 62.7, lease interest 25.6, total lease cash 95.9), diluted EPS table lines 6595-6601, shares on issue line 7927, borrowings 7820 and lease liabilities 8670
data_sources.qualitative: TWE.AX_Analysis.json (2026-11-08): FY27 guidance (EBITS at least FY26, ~A$40m Ascent savings, capex ~A$75m, leverage <2.0x by FY28, long-term EBITS margin 25%+), bull/bear points, RNDC exit, impairment history, CEO transition

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026 total revenue per metrics_normalized (NSR A$2,561m + other revenue). All margin paths are expressed on this total-revenue base, so the company's NSR-based EBITS margin (19.2% FY26) reads ~0.5pp lower here.
inputs.share_count_basis: 807.437m ordinary shares on issue at 30 June 2026 (FY26 AR note, line 7927) plus 2.757m potentially dilutive deferred shares (diluted EPS table, line 6599) = 810.2m fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would charge it twice.
inputs.net_debt_note: Total borrowings A$1,996.7m (FY26 AR line 7820) less lease liabilities A$465.5m (line 8670) = A$1,531.2m bonds/bank debt; less cash A$221.8m = A$1,309.4m. Lease liabilities are EXCLUDED here because leases are charged as an operating cost in the flows (treatment B). The company's own headline net debt of A$1,782.4m includes leases and is the covenant basis (2.8x EBITDAS).
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY26 owner FCF = OCF 190.4 - capex 113.3 (PP&E 110.7 + intangibles 2.6) - SBC 9.6 = 67.5. This is a TROUGH, not a base: FY26 OCF absorbed a A$326m working-capital build (inventories -165.3 incl. RNDC repurchased stock, payables -139.0) and A$108.8m net interest. The projection is component-built from EBITDAS, not extrapolated from this number. FY25 owner FCF was 369.8; FY22 439.4; five-year average FY22-26 ~A$223m levered, ~A$320m unlevered.
inputs.interest_income_note: Group 'finance income' of A$108.0m is the gross presentation of cross-currency swap/derivative income and is netted within net finance costs of A$107.4m; TWE is a net-debt company (no cash pile to double count), so no interest-income strip is made.
inputs.sbc_source: FY26 AR consolidated cash flow note, 'Share based payments expense' 9.6 (FY25 18.8), line 6660. No separate equity-award tax line disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0 in kpis), so the combined figure equals the add-back.
inputs.buyback_note: A$30.5m on-market buyback in H1 FY26 before the programme was cancelled at the February 2026 interim result. Buybacks are value-neutral in this model (count flat, SBC expensed); the flat count is a convention TWE is not currently funding.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in AUD, the currency of the flows. Risk-free: AUD 10y government ~4.4%. ERP 5.5%. Equity beta 1.05 (consumer staple with luxury-discretionary demand, US execution risk and leverage above target) gives cost of equity ~10.2%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.7% (FY26 net interest paid A$108.8m on ~A$1.9bn average gross debt), ~4.0% after 30% tax. Capital weights at market: equity A$5.1bn (6.35 x 810m), debt ex-leases A$1.3bn, so D/(D+E) ~20%. WACC = 0.80 x 10.2 + 0.20 x 4.0 = 9.0%. The elevated leverage (2.8x EBITDAS), Penfolds/China concentration and US impairment history are charged ONCE, in the flows: the bear path and a 30% bear weight, not an ad-hoc WACC premium, and the same 9.0% is used in all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: B - leases as operating cost. Total lease cash outflow A$95.9m FY26 (note 11(c): principal 70.3 + interest 25.6) is deducted inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path (3.65% of revenue, declining as surplus vineyard leases are exited - the A$109m FY26 write-down of land ROU assets signals that exit). D&A is ex right-of-use depreciation (165.3 - 62.7 = 102.6, 3.9% of revenue). Lease liabilities A$465.5m are excluded from net debt. Variable lease payments (A$142m) not in lease liabilities are already an expense inside EBITDAS.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests A$14.7m (book, FY26) deducted once in the equity bridge; flows are consolidated and not adjusted. Immaterial (~A$0.02/share).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing: operating company, non-US, cyclical consumer -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations). First valuation of this ticker; no prior DCF. BASE YEAR: FY2026 statutory NPAT of -A$1,077.8m is dominated by A$1,712m pre-tax material items (US goodwill/brand/PP&E/inventory write-downs on DAOU, Frank Family, Beaulieu, plus ROU write-downs); it is excluded entirely. The flows are built from EBITDAS (A$657.5m, 25.0% of revenue), which excludes material items and SGARA fair-value noise. FY26 EBITDAS margin is the trough of an eight-year 24.6-31.3% range (avg ~27%); the base case recovers to 28% by FY30, roughly mid-cycle plus a partial credit for the A$100m Ascent cost-out, and below management's 25%+ EBITS (~31% EBITDAS) aspiration. TAX: FY26 tax benefit was deferred-tax reversal on impaired intangibles, not a usable shelter; cash tax is modelled at 29% ramping to 30% (Australian statutory, where most profit sits). WORKING CAPITAL: wine inventory (~A$2bn) plus receivables far exceed payables, so growth consumes cash; wc_capture is negative (-35% base). Shrinkage in the bear case releases working capital, which the sign convention captures. DIVESTMENTS: proceeds from ongoing vineyard/brand sales (A$60.9m FY26) are not in the bridge; the commercial brands remain inside the flows at trough margins, so divestment proceeds are upside optionality, not modelled value. Dividend is suspended; deleveraging from 2.8x toward <2.0x by FY28 is consistent with the base-case unlevered FCF of A$370-400m less ~A$75m after-tax interest.

bear.narrative: The US division has not bottomed: further distributor disruption and category decline force more brand exits at distressed prices; Penfolds growth stalls on a China demand or trade-policy shock (anti-dumping duties of up to ~220% applied 2021-24 and could return); the commercial brands stay unsold and dilutive. Revenue falls a cumulative ~13% by FY29 and EBITDAS margin sits at FY21-type levels (24-25%) as cost-out only offsets negative operating leverage. Leverage stays above 2.0x past FY28 and the dividend remains suspended. Shrinkage releases some inventory, which the working-capital term captures.

base.narrative: FY27 follows guidance: revenue down ~3% as non-priority brands shrink and US luxury distributors destock, EBITS at least flat on FY26 (A$492m) with A$40m Ascent savings, capex ~A$75m. Margin recovers to 28% EBITDAS (about 22.5% EBITS on NSR) by FY30 as the remaining A$60m cost-out lands and Penfolds mix rises - mid-cycle, not the 25%+ EBITS target. Growth settles at 2.5-3%: Penfolds Asia growth less structural decline in US/ANZ volume.

bull.narrative: Ascent delivers in full: A$100m cost-out by FY29, portfolio down to ~30 brands with inventory release easing working capital, US destocking completes by 1H28 and Treasury Americas returns to growth off a written-down base, Penfolds China/Asia depletions keep compounding double-digit. EBITDAS margin reaches 31% (FY25's level, ~25% EBITS on NSR - management's target) by FY31 and holds.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30%: leverage is 2.8x EBITDAS against a <2.0x target with the dividend suspended and buyback cancelled (real balance-sheet strain, not conservatism); ~72% of divisional EBITS comes from one brand whose largest growth market applied ~220% duties as recently as 2021-24; the US division has been impaired repeatedly across FY26 with no confirmed bottom; and the 2025 commercial-brand sale failed for lack of buyers. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things to go right - full Ascent cost delivery, a US recovery and uninterrupted China growth - under a CEO one year into the role. Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
